evidence.ai_role: VISTA3D segments CT tumors; radiomic feature maps and CT inputs feed a 3D vision transformer for response prediction.
evidence.tested: Retrospective 517-patient three-center study: 185 development and 42 internal-test patients at A, 215 supervised-pretraining patients at B, 75 external-test patients at C. Source reports external AUC 0.81 with automated segmentation.
evidence.unknown: Clinical utility and causal adjuvant-treatment effects are unestablished. Internal-test segmentation-strategy selection is reported despite broader untouched-test claims.

organization: Shandong Cancer Hospital and Institute; West China Hospital, Sichuan University; Chinese Academy of Sciences; Peking University

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full XML: publication metadata, affiliations, Methods2.1 and model-development/segmentation sections, pCR Results and clinical limitations.

summary: A retrospective three-center study of 517 patients combined VISTA3D tumor segmentation with a 3D vision transformer to predict pathological complete response after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in non-small-cell lung cancer. Automated-segmentation predictions reached AUC 0.83 in the internal test and 0.81 in a 75-patient external center. Model-defined immune differences and apparent adjuvant-treatment survival associations were exploratory; they do not establish mechanism, causal treatment benefit or clinical utility. Small test cohorts and segmentation-strategy selection using internal-test performance limit interpretation; prospective validation remains needed.
title: CT deep learning predicts lung cancer treatment response
